---
title: "Wayward Book Mock"
subtitle: "A native Quarto book shell with Wayward styling"
---

This mock is meant to answer one question: what happens if we stop wrapping the
book in the website chrome and instead style Quarto's own book structure
directly?

## What this is testing

- the native Quarto sidebar as the real book navigation
- the native margin TOC as the real chapter navigation
- a Wayward visual system applied to those native components
- a page footer that belongs to the book layout rather than being injected by JS

## What this intentionally avoids

- moving DOM nodes after render
- rewriting links in JavaScript
- layering a second site shell on top of the book shell
- book-specific CSS fighting site-wide header and footer overrides

## The hypothesis

If this feels structurally cleaner, the next step is not "more overrides." It
is migrating the maths book to a dedicated format extension and letting the
extension own the book presentation from the start.
